definitions.explanation: A woman who has adopted a child through legal adoption, or a woman who raises a child that is not biologically hers. A formal term used in legal and family contexts.

examples.japanese: {養母|ようぼ}に{育|そだ}てられた。
examples.english: I was raised by my adoptive mother.

examples.japanese: {養母|ようぼ}と{実母|じつぼ}の{両方|りょうほう}に{感謝|かんしゃ}している。
examples.english: I am grateful to both my adoptive mother and my biological mother.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{幼|おさな}い{頃|ころ}に{養母|ようぼ}のもとに{引|ひ}き{取|と}られ、{大切|たいせつ}に{育|そだ}てられた。
examples.english: She was taken in by her adoptive mother when she was young and was raised with great care.

notes:
The formal term for an adoptive or foster mother. Part of a family of legal/formal kinship terms distinguishing biological from adoptive relationships.

RELATED FAMILY TERMS:
- {養父|ようふ}: adoptive father
- {養親|ようしん}: adoptive parent(s)
- {養子|ようし}: adopted child
- {実母|じつぼ}: biological mother
- {実父|じっぷ}: biological father

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {養母|ようぼ}に{育|そだ}てられる: to be raised by an adoptive mother
- {養母|ようぼ}のもとで: under the care of one's adoptive mother

USAGE:
A formal, written-style word most often seen in legal documents, official records, and narrative contexts (novels, biographical accounts). In everyday speech, people more commonly use {育|そだ}ての{親|おや} (the parent who raised me) or simply explain the relationship.

ETYMOLOGY:
{養|よう} (foster, raise, nurture) + {母|ぼ} (mother).
